positiveControlLedger.rule: a metric may gate a family only if it detects the strongest rung at >= 90 % on >= 8 trials; it informs where the strongest rung is above chance (one-sided exact p < 0.05); otherwise it is demoted for that family. Detected = strictly worse than the original in the metric's own direction.

humanAbControls.rule: sessionResults withholds Gate C unless sensitivityReport(session, independent votes, primary question).gate.verdict === may_judge_training; a session with no control pairs is withheld with that reason; control votes never enter the Elo, the tallies or the release share.
humanAbControls.route: POST /projects/{id}/listening-sessions builds the control pairs, degrades the challenger's own notes with degradeSideMidi (last track = the pitched track with the most notes; context bytes identical), renders original + degraded with LISTENING_SYNTH_V2 and stores them under the session (audioByToken). Not exercised against a live server in this stream.

honestLimits: shippedCriticScore equals criticScore within 0.11 on main 3bf23aa because the perform stage there does not repair notes and the critic is 76 % plan-derived; the inflation the audit describes becomes visible only once PR-98's playability repair merges (re-snapshot required: see the tracker entry for the command).

harmonyScore sits near its ceiling (98-100) on the synthetic corpus and the owner's song because the reference composer stacks chord tones (audit F6); the metric is discriminating (the tritone control drops it below 30) but not informative about label-stacking harmony. It measures chord membership and semitone clashes, not voice leading.

renderFailures = 5 on every case of the render baseline: every candidate's reference-synth render is reported infeasible by renderArrangementStems while the audio critic still scores it 87-93. Recorded, not investigated here (outside B-08's files).

seamArtefacts and trajectorySmoothness — two of the three coherence components now in the benchmark — detect no corruption family in the ledger; motifRecurrence and coherence.score inform only. They replace constants with measurements, not with validated gates.
candidateDistance ~ 6.6 (x100) on every case: the production gate's distance, whose plan-level components are empty on orchestrator output (plan.sections = []); only note-level components move.

The ledger's detection is a strict inequality on deterministic metrics; a gate verdict says the metric sees the damage, not that it sizes it. partJudge.score on arrangement anchors includes anchor-relative terms and is biased towards detection; its components are the honest rows.
musicCritic and candidateQuality run on Tier S anchors only (they need a plan); 13 candidateQuality dimensions are unavailable on brain output and are listed as insufficient data, not as demoted.
The Tier H task strips one family per task (N = 1); further stripping is implemented (stripAdditionalFamilies) but the committed run uses N = 1.

Gate C control pairs: with three pairs a session needs eight independent raters answering every pair before the gate can read both rungs (SENSITIVITY_GATE.minVotesPerRung = 8); the release share still needs five. The control pairs are rendered with LISTENING_SYNTH_V2 while the song pair plays the candidates' evaluation renders — one renderer within a pair, not across pairs.
The route wiring for control audio was typechecked, not run: no database or server in this stream.
No human has voted on any control pair; nothing here changes the training gate.

Tier H rights (corrected 2026-09-10): every entry now proves its composition — a verified composer dead by 1955 or a documented traditional tune — beside the uploader's public-domain statement for the score. Composer identification rests on PDMX's composer_name / artist_name as typed: a public-domain work whose row names nobody, or names its composer in a spelling the list lacks, is contested (under-admitted), never guessed in. 6,732 of 7,633 measured candidates are contested; 901 proven; 36 of the previous 40 entries and 49 of 54 tournament seeds are among the contested.

Tier H rights: a living arranger's CC0 arrangement of a public-domain composition is admitted on two facts (the uploader's dedication covers the arrangement layer; the composition basis covers the work); an arrangement of an unproven composition is contested whatever its score licence. A row naming a modern person beside a public-domain title is contested unless the name is a single word (an uploader handle), which does not block a verified title.

Tier H rights: the term applied is life + 70. Under the United States' publication-based term, works first published after 1929 by composers who died 1930–1955 may still be protected there; the corpus carries two Vierne entries (d. 1937) with composerDied > 1929 (listed under realCorpus.tierH.composerDeathYears.after1929) and the lead should decide whether to exclude them for a US-facing product.

Tier H cannot supply full_song / piano_vocal / vocal_only input types, electronic production, human gold arrangements — or, now, non-western idiom: no proven-public-domain multitrack work in PDMX carries a non-western genre / tag label (0 of 3, 7 gaps). Produced pop / dance / Mizrahi, electronic and other modern idioms cannot come from public-domain compositions at all; those rows of the required spread need licensed or operator-owned recordings. 'feel: swung' on this corpus is notated triplet subdivision in slow classical movements (Mozart K.467, Vivaldi, Verdi), not a jazz swing feel.

The first proven-only selection labelled three Christmas carols non_western through the bare substring 'world' matching tags such as 'joytotheworld'; the idiom regex is now bounded by non-letters and under-counts rather than invents. Duplicate arrangements of one composition are collapsed (one entry per composition).

rightsCorrection.ruling: The lead's ruling on B-08: a PDMX uploader's CC0 / public-domain statement clears at most the engraving or arrangement, never the composition. Tier H admits a work only when the composition is verifiably public domain (composer died in or before 1955 = life + 70 as of 2026, or a documented traditional / anonymous tune); everything else is rights.kind 'contested', commercialUse false, excluded from REAL_CORPUS_TIER_H and every Tier H aggregate, and listed with its reason. Contested / unknown are valid answers; no composer is guessed to admit a work.
rightsCorrection.mechanism: admit only what is proven: compositionRights.ts (a curated list of public-domain composers with death years and spellings met in PDMX, plus a curated list of verified traditional / public-domain tunes) read from the row's composer_name / artist_name / title; pdmxRightsBasis returns public_domain with composer + composerDied or traditional + source, else contested; benchmarkCorpusPlan.corpusRefusalReason refuses a public_domain basis with no composition evidence and any contested basis; selectTierH excludes before any quota is filled. No denylist of pop songs is used as the mechanism.

28 of 1,035 rows changed verdict; every one of them is a row with Tier S trials and the Tier H detected/trials of every changed row are identical to the previous ledger (the 80 Tier H anchors did not change). The changes are the merged brain's anchors, not the metrics or the corruptions.

Tier S anchors 9 → 8 (ethnic-vocal has no shipped arrangement to corrupt) and targets 40 → 31: B-01 removed the ensemble-transition track from every case and added keys to pop, ballad, rock, orchestral and cinematic; the lists are judged on 31 Tier S targets, still above the rule's 8 for every family that was judged before (candidateQuality.vocalFit / syncopation_removal fell to 6 trials and is insufficient_data).

Real losses on the merged anchors, demoted in the ledger and named here: musicCritic.playability gate → demoted on density_doubling (36/36 → 17/28, p 0.17) and role_inversion (25/25 → 11/15, p 0.06) — every one of the critic's 11 dimensions is now demoted, only musicCritic.overall gates (role_inversion) or informs (octave_displacement, density_doubling, duration_overhang); musicCritic.overall density_doubling gate → inform (33/36 → 20/28); candidateQuality.repetition bar_copy_repetition gate → inform (39/40 → 24/31); candidateQuality.vocalFit parallel_doubling inform → demoted (17/21 → 4/14), the dimension now demoted; partJudge.score octave_displacement inform → demoted (Tier S 24/29 → 10/21, Tier H 45/80 unchanged). No cause is isolated here; a control that varies one thing about the anchors would be needed before naming one.

Real gains on Tier S: candidateQuality.registerCollisions section_swap demoted → gate (18/40 → 29/31) and the dimension leaves the demoted list (octave_displacement, parallel_doubling inform); candidateQuality.score role_inversion inform → gate (18/25 → 14/15); coherence.harmonicAgreement on pitch_shift_out_of_key / chord_tone_to_non_chord_tone rose on Tier S (14/28 → 19/22, 18/28 → 20/21).

Gate verdicts gained on pooled rows where the Tier H part is unchanged and only the Tier S share moved: benchmarkHarmony.harmonyScore onset_jitter (95/107 → 91/100; Tier H 69/78 = 88.5 % on its own, below the gate; Tier S 22/22) — so 'nothing hears onset_jitter at gate level' is now 'harmonyScore gates it on the pooled trials and not on the human anchors alone'; benchmarkHarmony.clashShare leap_injection, bar_copy_repetition, duration_overhang; partJudge.score parallel_doubling; coherence.score pitch_shift_out_of_key; coherence.harmonicAgreement cross_part_clash. honestLimits: The 3bf23aa → 1467706 comparison is not a controlled experiment: five streams merged between the two snapshots and the corpus of selectable cases shrank from 9 to 8; the paired means are given, but no delta here isolates one stream.

gitSha in 1467706.json is the merge base, written with --git-sha; the run was taken from B-08 branch commit headSha, which differs from the base only in measurement, corpus, rights, listening-session and evidence files (git diff origin/main --stat touches no file on the arrangement path). A reader who wants the sha of the checkout that ran has it in headSha.

The benchmark's shape gained fields (unselectable, selectionReason, hardRule, unselectableShare, aggregateCases, headSha) without a version bump, so that 1467706.json remains comparable with 3bf23aa.json as asked; compareBenchmarkRuns takes the union of both files' metrics and shows a metric one file lacks as unavailable. A later reader should know that BENCHMARK_VERSION 2.0 covers both shapes.

ethnic-vocal's unselectability is reported, not repaired: the reference composer writes no bass or keys in that case's Chorus and Verse 2 although both are planned with chords under them; whether the plan or the composer is wrong is B-00/B-01's question.

Three of nine selected arrangements end after the Song Model's last bar (orchestral-midi +0.71 s, cinematic-midi +1.18 s, dance-full +0.24 s): a sustained final chord in the strings / keys / synth. Recorded from the test recalibration; not investigated; not B-08's file.

The ledger's Tier S losses (musicCritic.playability, candidateQuality.vocalFit and repetition, partJudge.score on octave_displacement) are stated as what the merged anchors show; nothing here says why the dimension stopped moving, and the corruption RNG stream is shared across anchors in order, so a Tier S row's exact counts depend on the anchor order as well as on the anchors.

Tier P (the owner's song) was orchestrated on the merged brain to check selectability (5 of 5 candidates pass the hard-rule gate, cand-D sparse selected) but was not re-snapshotted as a benchmark run in this commit.

pairedOverTheEightSelectableCases.note: 3bf23aa.json's aggregate covers 9 cases and the new file's covers 8 (ethnic-vocal is unselectable now), so the CLI's aggregate deltas mix a corpus change with a composer change. These are the means of both files over the same 8 cases.
